Categories.value: Taken with Nikon D5000|Canada Olympic Park|Flickr images reviewed by File Upload Bot (Magnus Manske)|Files from InSapphoWeTrust Flickr stream|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Canada photographs taken on 2012-07-24|Views of Calgary

ImageDescription.value:
I had expected Calgary to be rather underwhelming due to its prairie location, and never really allotted much time to it at all. Besides, with my border delays on my way into Canada, I had to hurriedly skip Calgary on my way to the Rockies.

But after I wrapped up my Rockies sightseeing, instead of proceeding west immediately to Vancouver, I backtracked an hour east back to Calgary, in order to get some photo angles and get at least a teaser of what the city has to offer.

With Bow River flowing through city center and nice hills to the west, Calgary is more scenic than I had expected. Here, I managed to take this shot of downtown, from Canada Olympic Park to the west, in particular the Ski Jump Tower for the 1988 Winter Olympics, Calgary's highest vantage point. I am loving what I'm seeing.

ImageDescription.value: Canada Olympic Park, located in western Calgary on a hill, is a great place to take in city views and explore the legacy of Canadian Olympic sports. Here is a look at some of the participating nations' flags from the 1988 Winter Olympics. The presence of Soviet and Yugoslavian flags is particularly notable, since both nations disbanded in 1991, and Calgary ended up being the final winter appearance for both traditional Olympic powerhouses.
